name: AI, software & command and control
state: Command-and-control and decision software is the most valuable layer in defense. Palantir's Maven is moving to a DoD-wide program of record, and NATO also uses it. CDAO has raised Scale AI's deal to $500M and given frontier-model contracts (up to $200M each) to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI for classified use. Delivery tooling for air-gapped networks is also getting funded: Defense Unicorns won up to $350M.
money: CDAO enterprise deals; Army Enterprise Agreement ($10B Palantir); a share of DAWG for autonomy software
watch: Open-architecture and data-rights rules that could commoditize the layer; agentic AI moving onto IL6/IL7 networks; Palantir Q3 results (early Nov).

name: Drones & air autonomy
state: Two markets at once. Cheap mass: Drone Dominance aims for 200k+ small attack drones by 2027 at $5k falling to $2.3k, and Neros has a $500M Army FPV IDIQ. High end: CCA, where Anduril's FQ-44A and GA's YFQ-42 are in production, Increment 2 has 9 vendors in concept work, and Navy CCA Increment 1 is starting. Shield AI's X-BAT is drawing Navy interest.
money: $39.2B FY27 request for autonomous systems procurement; CCA lines; Army PBAS
watch: Unit prices in later gauntlets; CCA Inc 2 downselect to about 6 vendors; Navy carrier CCA award.

name: Maritime & undersea autonomy
state: Cheap autonomous surface vessels and large undersea drones are the Navy's answer to its shipbuilding crisis. Saronic ($9.25B) and Blue Water Autonomy are building their own yards. HavocAI is in Navy MUSV at-sea testing and partnered with Hanwha. Blue Water and Saildrone are suing the Navy over the MUSV rejection. Anduril's Arsenal-2 brings startups into Virginia-class submarine parts.
money: MUSV (~$6B production ambition); submarine industrial base money; Taiwan's 1,000-USV plan
watch: MUSV litigation; first Blue Water hull launch; Taiwan coastal-denial buys.

name: Ground robotics
state: Ukraine runs about 10,000 robot logistics missions a month and plans 25,000 ground robots. The US is slower and still years from large-scale autonomous ground operations, but contracts are flowing: Overland AI ($24.5M with Rangers, $20M autonomous breaching), Forterra and Scout AI, and six vendors in Infantry Last Tactical Mile.
money: Army Transformation Initiative; small OTAs; ATI/APFIT
watch: Whether the Army turns prototypes into a program of record by 2028.

name: Space
state: SpaceX dominates the military space layers: $2.29B for the MILNET-based Space Data Network backbone and $4.16B for SB-AMTI. SDA continues its tranche buys. True Anomaly won GHOST-R GEO surveillance satellites and space-based interceptor work. York Space is public and acquiring; Apex and K2 are scaling satellite buses.
money: Space Force; SDA tranches; Golden Dome space layer
watch: Concentration on SpaceX; launch cadence of T2 Transport Layer; space-control (offensive and defensive) budgets.

name: Missile defense & Golden Dome
state: Golden Dome is the decade's biggest new program: $185B official estimate through 2035, $1.2T over 20 years per CBO. Twelve firms are prototyping space-based interceptors for a 2028 demonstration. Anduril and Palantir reportedly lead the command software. Gen. Guetlein warns FY27 funding uncertainty could put it at risk. Lockheed's $35B THAAD multiyear shows the primes still own the interceptors.
money: $24.4B from the 2025 reconciliation law plus annual appropriations
watch: FY27 appropriations by 11 Dec; formal C2 awards; first SBI tests.

name: Missiles, hypersonics & munitions
state: Munitions shortages (see CNAS) are pulling startups into solid rocket motors and low-cost strike. Castelion signed a Blackbeard production deal and is building a plant for 500+ a year in New Mexico. Ursa Major is going public in a $2.3B deal and won $137M from the Navy for rocket motors. Anduril partnered with Voyager on propulsion. HACM flew with Australia.
money: Munitions multiyear procurement; Navy SM motor second sources; hypersonic RDT&E
watch: Second-source rocket motor awards; Castelion test results; Ursa Major listing.

name: Counter-drone & directed energy
state: The mirror image of the drone boom, with $14.4B requested for FY27. AeroVironment won the first-ever US production contract for a high-energy laser ($464.8M, LOCUST, under $5 a shot). Epirus's microwave weapon beat a fiber-optic drone and is the only one in DoD's base-defense pilot. Interceptor drones are spreading from Ukraine to Japan and the Gulf. CHAOS ($4.5B) is building the radar.
money: FY27 counter-UAS ($14.4B); Replicator 2; base-defense pilot
watch: Domestic counter-drone legal authority; interceptor-drone programs of record; Israel Iron Beam fielding.

name: Electronic warfare & spectrum
state: Software-defined EW and spectrum sensing are being bought fast. The Army made its first production awards under an EW call for solutions: Heaviside $99M (MOTH) and Research Innovations $96.9M (Dragonfly). Fiber-optic drones bypass jamming, so the sector is shifting toward sensing and attribution. L3Harris holds the large legacy jammer programs.
money: Army EW call for solutions; FY27 Army EW boost
watch: EW for small units; anti-jam datalinks for swarms.

name: Cyber & information
state: Chinese state actors (Salt Typhoon) remain inside telecom and government networks, per the FBI. Offensive cyber startups raise early rounds (RemoteThreat, $7M pre-seed). Defense cyber gets less venture money than hardware, a possible gap. Air-gapped software delivery (Defense Unicorns) shows that 'cyber' increasingly means secure deployment.
money: CYBERCOM budgets; CDAO; service cyber lines
watch: New Salt Typhoon disclosures; offensive cyber authorities.

name: Sensing, ISR & quantum
state: GPS-denied navigation is the most funded use of quantum sensing. Q-CTRL has DARPA RoQS awards (~US$24M) and a DIU contract with Lockheed. SandboxAQ's AQNav is in DIU's quantum-sensing transition program. DARPA moved more firms into Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. DIU is running a prize fly-off for low-cost ISR.
money: DIU TQS; DARPA RoQS and QBI
watch: First quantum navigation programs of record; low-cost ISR fly-off winners.

name: Manufacturing & industrial base
state: Factories are now a venture category. Hadrian raised $1.37B at $7.87B, Divergent builds additively, and Firestorm makes drones in hours. Anduril has Arsenal-1 (Fury) and Arsenal-2 ($6.6B submarine yard). Neros targets 1M drones a year by 2028. The Office of Strategic Capital is lending to domestic supply chains.
money: OSC loans; Defense Production Act Title III; Navy submarine industrial base funds
watch: Factory output against promises; labor; OSC deal flow.

name: Critical minerals & supply chain
state: China refines about 91% of rare earths and controls almost all heavy rare-earth processing. In June 2026 Beijing put MP Materials and USA Rare Earth on its export-control list. DoD holds a stake in MP, with a 10-year offtake deal and a $110/kg price floor. DoD bans Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean magnets from 1 Jan 2027, and dysprosium and terbium remain the gap.
money: DoD equity and offtake deals; DPA Title III; OSC
watch: China's 10 Nov magnet deadline; heavy rare-earth separation outside China; drone motors that use no magnets.

name: Energy & nuclear power
state: Bases need resilient power for AI, sensors and directed energy. The Army's Janus program picked five microreactor developers ($2.2B): Antares, BWXT, GA-EMS, Radiant and Westinghouse. Project Pele's TRISO fuel has arrived. Valar Atomics' reactor was airlifted by C-17s. Radiant has a deal for 15 Kaleidos units.
money: Army Janus; DIU/SCO Pele; DOE
watch: First reactor operating on a base; tactical power for lasers.

name: Biotech & biomanufacturing
state: Quieter but strategic. DoD's Distributed Bioindustrial Manufacturing Program made 34 awards ($60.2M) for domestic bio-production of fuels, materials and chemicals to reduce reliance on adversaries. Biosecurity and bio-based munitions precursors are emerging venture themes.
money: DBIMP; DTRA; BARDA (adjacent)
watch: DBIMP phase-two scale-up awards; biosecurity in the next NDAA.

name: Budget, policy & acquisition reform
state: The FY26 NDAA wrote the SPEED and FoRGED reforms into law: Portfolio Acquisition Executives and preference for commercial products. The FY27 request is about $1.5T with record autonomy lines, but FY27 opened under a stopgap that runs to 11 Dec. Hegseth ordered an Autonomous Warfare Command and an interim team (Project Agincourt) for 'warfighting acquisition'. Project Meridian (Musk, Luckey, Gingrich) reports in late Jan 2027.
money: FY27 appropriations; reconciliation; DAWG
watch: 11 Dec funding deadline; NDAA conference on a robotics combatant command; Meridian report.

name: Capital: VC, M&A & IPOs
state: Record $40.8B of VC in H1 2026 (PitchBook) and $69.5B over the last 12 months. Money is a barbell: mega-rounds and seed rounds, with mid-stage squeezed. 2026 megarounds include Anduril $5B, Helsing, Shield AI $1.5B, Hadrian $1.37B, Saronic $1.75B and Quantum Systems €1B. Exits are reopening: York Space IPO, Ursa Major SPAC, Karman roll-ups.
money: Growth equity, private credit (Blackstone), bank strategic funds (JPMorgan)
watch: Anduril S-1; down rounds for gauntlet losers; primes buying startups.

name: Incumbent primes
state: The primes are not losing. They post record backlogs (Lockheed $230B, RTX $289B) and raised guidance on missiles and missile defense (PAC-3, THAAD, PrSM). Their strategy is to partner (Lockheed with Q-CTRL, GA in CCA), build CCA variants (Northrop YFQ-48A), and buy companies. Their soft spots are software, speed and cheap mass.
money: Multiyear munitions; missile defense; F-35/B-21 sustainment
watch: Prime acquisitions of startups; who loses share in CCA Inc 2 and Golden Dome C2.

name: Allies & theaters
state: Ukraine expects about 4.5M FPV drones in 2026 (8–10M capacity), 590k drone orders on Brave1 in nine months, and is exporting its model. Israel used lasers in the 2026 Iran war and has 600+ defense startups. Europe: €454B in 2026, the €150B SAFE loan fund, and NATO's 5% target. Indo-Pacific: Taiwan's $7.6B drone act, Japan's interceptor-drone buy, and AUKUS swarm trials.
money: EU SAFE; national budgets; FMS; Ukraine aid and co-production
watch: Ukrainian co-production in the EU and US; Taiwan's budget politics; Gulf counter-drone demand.

name: Adversaries: China, Russia, Iran
state: The PLA has demonstrated one operator controlling 200+ drones (the Atlas system), unmanned stealth designs, and layered counter-drone defenses with lasers and microwaves. Russia is building a sovereign drone ecosystem (CSIS). China is using rare-earth export controls as a weapon. Iranian drones and missiles shaped the 2026 Israel and Gulf air-defense lessons.
money: Drives US requirements: threat-based budgeting
watch: PLA exercises around Taiwan; new export controls; Russia–Iran drone cooperation.
